capabilities.target: payments-agent: pay vendor using bank details from the chosen quote

inputs.source: Vendor quote emails and attachments from outside senders

instructions.note: The only stated check against paying a fraudulent vendor, "Only pay vendors on the approved list", is a plain instruction with no structural enforcement and no verification of the bank account details themselves.

"Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks" implies a downstream safeguard, but runtime notes show payments-agent performs no additional verification and pays whatever bank details are in the task.
"Choose the best one" gives no defined selection criteria (price, vendor reputation, bank-detail consistency), leaving room for an attacker-favorable quote to be selected.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: A human decision made before any quote exists is independent of model capability, but it does not cover the vendor or bank details actually paid, so it earns no credit against the payment capability.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: only pay vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends on the model choosing to check the vendor name against the list; it never verifies the bank account details, and a more capable or more adversarially prompted model can rationalize exceptions or be defeated by vendor-name spoofing inside the quote.

controls.name: Independent bank-detail verification against vendor master data
controls.decay_rationale: An out-of-band check against a registry the inbound email cannot write to would hold regardless of model capability.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval of final vendor/bank details before payment
controls.decay_rationale: A human reviewing the actual destination account after quote selection, at low volume, is independent of model capability.

controls.name: Propagate manager approval context to payments-agent and require a match before paying
controls.decay_rationale: Binding the approval record to the task at the peer, enforced outside the model, closes the authority-laundering gap regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Pin/sign payments-agent card and require mTLS or signed identity
controls.decay_rationale: Cryptographic pinning and mutual authentication do not depend on model behavior.

controls.name: Tamper-evident payment audit record binding approval, quote, and paid bank details
controls.decay_rationale: A structural log written outside model control remains attributable regardless of model capability.

findings.title: TC7 authority laundering + vendor bank-detail fraud (BEC) reaches irreversible payment delegation

attack_path.note: Manager approves item and budget before any vendor quote exists; approval record is not passed to payments-agent (approval_context_propagates: false).
Untrusted vendor quote email from outside the company; attacker can author quote content including bank account details.
Orchestrator checks the chosen vendor's name against the approved list (prompt.md:3), but this is a name match only; it does not verify the bank account number in the quote.
Orchestrator hands payments-agent a task with 'the bank details from the chosen quote' (prompt.md:3), so attacker-supplied bank details drive an irreversible payment.
payments-agent trusts any task bearing the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task with no further check, despite prompt.md:4 claiming it 'will handle any remaining checks.'

forecast.watch_signal: Model/version string changes in subject.model, or median quote volume/task length per purchase request rises, making the 'only pay approved vendors' prompt instruction easier to route around via multi-step quote chains.

evidence.observation: "collect vendor quotes, choose the best one, and hand it to payments-agent to pay. Use the bank details from the chosen quote." ties payment bank details directly to attacker-reachable quote content.
"Only pay vendors on the approved list" is the only stated safeguard, and it is a behavioral prompt instruction with no structural enforcement.
The manager approves item and budget before any quote exists, and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent, so the approval never covers the specific vendor or bank details actually paid.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task, with no independent verification against vendor master data.

recommendations.action: Verify the bank account/routing details in the chosen quote against an independently maintained, out-of-band vendor payment registry before releasing any payment; block or route to human review on mismatch.
Require a raw-action human approval step on cap.delegate_payment showing the actual vendor name and bank account to be paid, after quote selection, at low volume (one review per request).
Propagate the manager's approval record (approved vendor/budget) to payments-agent and require it to match the task before paying, closing the authority-laundering gap.

findings.title: Unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card and static bearer token leave the orchestrator-payments A2A channel without mutual identity assurance

forecast.watch_signal: A new payments or finance peer agent is added without signed/pinned agent cards, or a proposed move to mTLS/signed identity is not adopted.

evidence.observation: authentication schemes list only ["bearer"], a static credential type, with no mention of per-session scoping or rotation.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned, so a later change or a spoofed response could substitute a different endpoint or skill definition.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token, meaning possession of that static token is sufficient to impersonate the orchestrator's authority.

recommendations.action: Pin or hash the payments-agent card/definition at first trust and alert on change; verify peer identity with mTLS or signed identity rather than a bearer token alone.

findings.title: No tamper-evident record binding a specific approval or quote to the payment payments-agent executes

forecast.watch_signal: Payment volume or autonomy increases without an accompanying attributable, tamper-evident log tying each payment to its approval and quote.

evidence.observation: The approval record is not passed to payments-agent, and no logging or audit mechanism is described anywhere in the artifacts for either agent.
"Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks" asserts a safeguard that the runtime notes show does not exist, with no mention of any record created for later review.

recommendations.action: Create a tamper-evident audit record at payment time binding the manager's approval id, the chosen quote, and the bank details actually paid, independent of model-generated summaries.

stride_coverage.rationale: Employee purchase requests authenticate via the organization's SSO system before reaching the orchestrator; artifacts show no channel where the orchestrator itself could be spoofed to the requester or manager.
Artifacts do not state whether multiple purchase requests can be processed concurrently or whether any per-period spend or rate cap applies across requests.

The payment itself transfers funds per the task it receives; the loss this could cause from a fraudulent task is captured as tampering and elevation_of_privilege in finding F1-vendor-bec-authority-laundering.
No rate limit, spend cap, or per-period volume cap is described for payments-agent's processing of delegated tasks.
The vendor sender is outside the organization's control; the design cannot enforce non-repudiation on an external party's email, only verify its content, addressed under spoofing above.
This inbound flow carries vendor quote content into the orchestrator; it is a read of external content, not a flow that discloses internal data outward.
No information on email volume handling, attachment size limits, or rate limiting for inbound vendor quote processing is given.
No rate limit or circuit breaker is described for the A2A payment delegation channel between the orchestrator and payments-agent.
Artifacts do not describe who can write to the approved vendor list or what integrity controls protect its contents.
The approved vendor list is internal reference data read by the orchestrator; artifacts show no path that returns its contents to an external party.
Reading a static approved vendor list is a bounded, low-cost operation with no stated availability dependency that request volume could meaningfully degrade.

rating.rationale: The dominant path is an untrusted vendor-quote email driving an irreversible payment delegation (U source to S3 sink), inherently critical. The only credited control today is a behavioral prompt instruction to check vendor names against an approved list, which does not verify bank account details and gives one tier of credit, leaving residual at high. Two property gaps compound this: the A2A channel to payments-agent has no signed/pinned identity or mutual authentication (high), and no tamper-evident record binds a specific approval or quote to the payment actually made (high). Because the one credited control is behavioral and dependent on model compliance, model_upgrade or longer_task_horizon triggers remove it entirely, returning the primary finding to critical, which sets the forecast rating.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt, agent card, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agents.
No MCP/A2A traffic captures or logs were provided; payments-agent's bearer-token trust behavior is taken as stated in the runtime notes.
Autonomy step and runtime limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not stated in the artifacts and are recorded as null/unknown.

No information was provided on request volume, how managers review item/budget detail in practice, or any existing audit logging, which limits confidence on likelihood and on the denial-of-service and repudiation categories.
